name: Shackleton Crater Rim
description: Perched on the towering rim crest of the 21-km diameter Shackleton Crater, less than 5 km from the precise South Pole. Experiences near-perpetual solar grazing for Artemis solar towers, while the crater interior drops 4.2 km into cryogenic cold traps harboring volatile water ice.

name: Connecting Ridge
description: A prominent elevated ridge connecting the rims of Shackleton and De Gerlache craters. Features gentle slopes (<6°) ideal for lunar lander touchdown and long-duration solar illumination during southern summer.

name: Malapert Massif
description: Standing over 5,000 meters above the lunar datum, Malapert Massif provides near-continuous line of sight with Earth for Direct-To-Earth (DTE) radio communications. Its elevated horizon vantage point is immune to crater shadowing towards the north.

name: Nobile Rim 1 (VIPER / Griffin)
description: Designated by NASA as the primary landing zone for the VIPER ice-mapping rover and Astrobotic Griffin lander. Features broad, manageable trafficability for rovers and convenient proximity to small micro-PSRs containing volatile deposits.

name: Haworth Crater Ridge
description: Located on the ridge bordering Haworth Crater, which harbors surface temperatures as cold as 35 Kelvin (-400°F). Holds immense scientific value for water ice analysis, but presents extreme crater rim shadowing.

name: Leibnitz Beta Plateau
description: A high lunar massif ridge offering expansive views over the polar crater clusters, moderate landing plains, high solar availability, and stable Direct-To-Earth telecommunications.

name: IM-1 Odysseus (Malapert A)
description: Landing site of the historic Intuitive Machines IM-1 Odysseus mission (February 2024), the first American commercial lunar lander to touch down on the Moon. Demonstrates sub-polar communications and lighting challenges.

name: IM-2 PRIME-1 (Connecting Ridge Drill)
description: Target site for Intuitive Machines IM-2 carrying NASA's Polar Resources Ice Mining Experiment-1 (PRIME-1) regolith ice drill and mass spectrometer.

name: Firefly Blue Ghost 1 (Mare Crisium)
description: Selected landing site for Firefly Aerospace's Blue Ghost CLPS lander inside the basaltic plain of Mare Crisium. Demonstrates equatorial lunar lighting with 14 Earth days of continuous sunlight followed by 14 Earth days of night.

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti Point)
description: Historic touchdown site of India's Vikram lander and Pragyan rover (ISRO Chandrayaan-3, August 2023). First spacecraft to land in the lunar southern high-latitude highland plains.

name: Apollo 11 (Statio Tranquillitatis)
description: The first human landing site on another celestial body (July 20, 1969). Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin stepped onto the lunar surface here. Demonstrates equatorial lunar day/night cycles with high Sun elevations (>80°).

name: Apollo 17 (Taurus-Littrow Valley)
description: Last Apollo human lunar landing site (December 1972) by Gene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt. Located in a narrow valley flanked by the towering North and South Massifs that rose 2,000 meters above the valley floor.

name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán Crater)
description: First ever soft landing on the far side of the Moon (CNSA, January 2019). Because Earth is permanently occulted by the Moon's bulk (Earth Elevation = -135°), direct communication is impossible; all signals require the Queqiao relay satellite.

name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo Crater Basin)
description: Touchdown site of Chang'e 6 (June 2024), which retrieved the first historic soil and rock samples from the Moon's ancient far side South Pole-Aitken basin.

name: JAXA SLIM (Shioli Crater)
description: Touchdown site of Japan's 'Moon Sniper' SLIM lander (January 2024), achieving pinpoint landing within 55 meters on a steep 15-degree crater slope.
